Tiny habits that
make you sharper by 30
Doing mental maths instead of reaching for the calculator. Splitting a bill, working out a discount. Small daily practice keeps your brain quick.
Learning the route instead of following the GPS. Finding your way through a city trains memory and attention in a way a screen never will.
Reading long articles all the way to the end. Training your attention span on real content is the opposite of endless short videos.
Playing strategy games with friends. Chess, card games, board games. Thinking two moves ahead is a skill that grows with practice.
Learning something new every day. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and small daily lessons keep my mind quick and curious.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Small daily lessons keep my mind quick and curious.

slides.texte_overlay: Explaining what you learned to someone else. If you can teach it simply, you really understand it, and it stays in your memory for good.
Sleeping seven to eight hours. Your brain sorts and stores everything you learned while you sleep. Short nights quietly make you slower.
